instruction: Go to the recreation.gov homepage and verify that the main search input field is present on the page.

metadata.explanation: Task variation that verifies the user has successfully navigated to the recreation.gov homepage. Uses existing Chrome getters (active_tab_info) and metrics (is_expected_url_pattern_match) to check if the URL contains 'recreation.gov'. This is a simpler variation focusing on URL navigation verification.

llm_judge_reasons: Incomplete verification coverage: Instruction has TWO requirements (1. navigate to recreation.gov homepage, 2. verify search input field is present), but evaluator only checks requirement #1
The metric 'is_expected_url_pattern_match' only validates URL pattern matching via regex 'recreation\.gov' and completely ignores page content

The getter 'active_tab_info' actually retrieves page HTML content (url, title, content fields), which COULD be used to verify the search input field presence, but the metric doesn't use this content field

Instruction-evaluator semantic mismatch: The instruction explicitly asks to 'verify that the main search input field is present on the page', but no part of the evaluator checks for page elements or DOM structure
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Option 1: Simplify the instruction to match what the evaluator actually checks - change to: 'Go to the recreation.gov homepage' (remove the search input field verification requirement)

Option 2: Update the evaluator to check BOTH requirements - use a metric that can parse page content to verify the presence of search input field (e.g., check for input element with id='hero-search-input' or similar selector in the HTML content)
Option 3: Use a different metric like 'check_page_element_exists' that can validate DOM elements by parsing the 'content' field returned by active_tab_info getter
